short_description: ABS controller auxiliary I/O circuit (I/O 2 or I/O 3) shorted high
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 154 (ABS controller auxiliary I/O circuit) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the ABS/ESC on a configurable auxiliary output driver -- wired at the factory to a differential lock, transfer case, trailer, or a general-purpose 3/2 valve solenoid -- when that output circuit reads shorted to voltage or ground, open, or does not match its parameter-set configuration. Diagnosis follows the wiring for whichever solenoid the output is assigned to on this vehicle.
source_doc: SD-13-4983 EC-80 ABS/ATC service data sheet (2014)

short_description: Wheel speed sensor, steer axle left, sensor air gap too large
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 789 (Wheel speed sensor, steer axle left) with FMI 1 (Reading in-range but far too low) is set by the ABS/ESC when the wheel-speed sensor's air gap to the tone ring is outside its working range, or wheel-end bearing play has grown enough to affect the reading. WABCO and Bendix both specify a nominal 0.4 mm (0.016 in) sensor-to-tone-wheel gap; a gap that is too wide, a damaged tone ring, or excess wheel-bearing play all produce this fault.
source_doc: SD-13-4983 EC-80 ABS/ATC service data sheet (2014)

short_description: Wheel speed sensor, additional axle right, sensor air gap too large
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 794 (Wheel speed sensor, additional axle right) with FMI 1 (Reading in-range but far too low) is set by the ABS/ESC when the wheel-speed sensor's air gap to the tone ring is outside its working range, or wheel-end bearing play has grown enough to affect the reading. WABCO and Bendix both specify a nominal 0.4 mm (0.016 in) sensor-to-tone-wheel gap; a gap that is too wide, a damaged tone ring, or excess wheel-bearing play all produce this fault.
source_doc: SD-13-4983 EC-80 ABS/ATC service data sheet (2014)

short_description: Wheel speed sensor wiring swapped left/right on an axle
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 810 (Wheel speed sensors reversed on axle (configuration)) with FMI 7 (Mechanical part not reacting or misadjusted) is set by the ABS/ESC when a wheel-speed signal is plausible in amplitude but behaves erratically -- chattering, jumping, arriving at the wrong update rate, or disagreeing with the other wheels on the axle, including a sensor pair wired in reverse or an output too low at drive-off. Typical causes are a damaged or debris-packed tone ring, a loose sensor, mismatched tire sizes on an axle, or a mis-wired sensor after a service.
source_doc: SD-13-4983 EC-80 ABS/ATC service data sheet (2014)

short_description: Hill start assist lamp circuit open or shorted to ground
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 2622 (Hill start assist (HSA) valve/lamp circuit) with FMI 2 (Signal unstable, intermittent or implausible) is set by the ABS/ESC when the hill-start-assist (HSA) lamp or holding-valve solenoid circuit reads open or shorted. HSA briefly holds air pressure at the service brakes on a grade; a failed lamp driver or solenoid coil, or a broken wire, prevents it from working correctly.
source_doc: SD-13-4983 EC-80 ABS/ATC service data sheet (2014)

short_description: Parameter 2970 (validation switch) signal erratic, intermittent or implausible
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 2970 (Parameter 2970 (role not stated by the OEM tables)) with FMI 2 (Signal unstable, intermittent or implausible) is set by the Engine ECU when the accelerator pedal position sensor signal is missing, out of range or implausible relative to the engine's other timing references. Typical causes are a failed sensor, an incorrect air gap, connector corrosion, chafed wiring, or damage to the toothed wheel the sensor reads.
source_doc: 1200 Series marine auxiliary engines troubleshooting guide

short_description: Fuel rail pressure sensor circuit reads low (shorted to ground)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 157 (Fuel rail pressure) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU when the fuel rail (common rail) pressure sensor signal leaves its plausible window or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. Typical causes are a failed sensor, corroded connector pins, chafed harness wiring, or a genuine underlying system condition the sensor is correctly reporting.
source_doc: A042J565 fire pump drive engine IOM, fault code charts

short_description: Injector solenoid, cylinder 1, circuit open (no current)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 651 (Injector cylinder 1) with FMI 5 (Current too low; open circuit) is set by the Engine ECU when the fuel injector driver circuit reads an abnormal current, resistance or calibration value. Typical causes are a failed injector coil/solenoid, a chafed or corroded driver circuit, or an injector trim code that was not carried over after replacement.
source_doc: A042J565 fire pump drive engine IOM, fault code charts

short_description: Cylinder 4 exhaust temperature, right bank, far above normal
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1146 (Cylinder 4 exhaust temperature, right bank) with FMI 0 (Reading in-range but far too high) is set by the Engine ECU when the cylinder misfire/power-balance monitor fails to reach or hold the commanded position/pressure. Typical causes are a sticking or contaminated valve, a failed valve body, or an upstream system-pressure problem.
source_doc: A042J565 fire pump drive engine IOM, fault code charts

short_description: Intake manifold air temperature reads in-range but abnormally high
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 105 (Intake manifold air temperature) with FMI 0 (Reading in-range but far too high) is set by the Aftertreatment DCU for an engine pressure or temperature parameter (fuel delivery pressure, oil pressure, boost pressure, intake manifold temperature, air filter differential pressure, barometric pressure, coolant temperature, ambient air temperature, or turbocharger compressor inlet pressure) that the aftertreatment DCU consumes for its own dosing and regeneration strategy and relays into this fault list. Diagnose it as an ordinary pressure/temperature sensor circuit: connector, wiring, then sensor.
source_doc: DTC list MD1 DOC/DPF (2019)

short_description: TSC1 (torque/speed control) message receive timeout reads in-range but abnormally high
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3349 (TSC1 (torque/speed control) message receive timeout) with FMI 0 (Reading in-range but far too high) is set by the Aftertreatment DCU when a J1939 message the aftertreatment control system depends on -- a torque/speed command (TSC1), a NOx or urea-quality sensor reading, or the data-verification handshake with the engine ECU -- stops arriving at the expected rate or fails validation. Typical causes are the sending sensor or ECU losing power or ground, a connector or backbone fault between the DCU and the sending node, or the sending device itself faulting.
source_doc: DTC list MD1 DOC/DPF (2019)

short_description: EGR valve actuator position circuit voltage reads low (shorted to ground)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 27 (EGR valve actuator position) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU when the EGR valve actuator will not reach or hold a commanded position, reports an internal fault, loses calibration, or the motor coil circuit is open or shorted. Carbon buildup in the valve bore that increases actuator load is a leading mechanical cause behind an electrical-looking fault.
source_doc: DTC list EMR5 / MD1 (2026-07-22)

short_description: Throttle valve position sensor fault detected, cause undetermined
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 51 (Throttle valve position sensor) with FMI 11 (Fault detected, cause undetermined) is set by the Engine ECU when the throttle position sensor signal is missing, out of range or implausible relative to the engine's other timing references. Typical causes are a failed sensor, an incorrect air gap, connector corrosion, chafed wiring, or damage to the toothed wheel the sensor reads.
source_doc: KWP list EMR4 (2026-06-10)

short_description: Engine oil pressure signal erratic, intermittent or implausible
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 100 (Engine oil pressure) with FMI 2 (Signal unstable, intermittent or implausible) is set by the Engine ECU when the engine oil pressure sensor signal leaves its plausible window or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. Typical causes are a failed sensor, corroded connector pins, chafed harness wiring, or a genuine underlying system condition the sensor is correctly reporting.
source_doc: KWP list EMR4 (2026-06-10)

short_description: Barometric pressure sensor circuit reads low (shorted to ground)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 108 (Barometric pressure sensor) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU when the ambient/barometric pressure sensor signal leaves its plausible window or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. Typical causes are a failed sensor, corroded connector pins, chafed harness wiring, or a genuine underlying system condition the sensor is correctly reporting.
source_doc: KWP list EMR4 (2026-06-10)

short_description: Engine coolant level sensor reads moderately above the normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 171 (Engine coolant level sensor) with FMI 16 (Moderately above normal range) is set by the Engine ECU when the engine coolant level sensor reads an implausible level or an out-of-range circuit. Typical causes are a genuinely low/high fluid level, a failed level sensor/float, or a chafed sensor circuit.
source_doc: DTC list EMR5 / MD1 (2026-07-22)

short_description: Clutch pedal switch value is changing implausibly fast or slow
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 598 (Clutch pedal switch) with FMI 10 (Value changing implausibly fast or slow) is set by the Engine ECU when a discrete switch input (a clutch, neutral, lock, mode, power, or similar panel or chassis switch) reads a state the ESC considers implausible, or a switch is found stuck in one position against the vehicle's actual operating state. Typical causes are a worn or failed switch, a corroded connector or pin, or an open or shorted signal wire between the switch and the body controller.
source_doc: DTC list EMR5 / MD1 (2026-07-22)

short_description: Engine control unit internal fault component reports an internal failure
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 629 (Engine control unit internal fault) with FMI 12 (Smart device or component defective) is set by the Engine ECU when it detects an internal fault in its own memory, software or supply. Typical causes are a corrupted calibration, a power/ground fault at the ECU connector, or, rarely, a failed ECU that needs dealer replacement and reprogramming.
source_doc: DTC list EMR5 / MD1 (2026-07-22)

short_description: Injector cylinder 4 circuit shorted to battery
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 654 (Injector cylinder 4) with FMI 8 (Wrong frequency, pulse width or period) is set by the Engine ECU when the fuel injector driver circuit reads an abnormal current, resistance or calibration value. Typical causes are a failed injector coil/solenoid, a chafed or corroded driver circuit, or an injector trim code that was not carried over after replacement.
source_doc: DTC list EMRL1 main + secondary ECU

short_description: Fuel injection pump metering valve circuit shorted to battery (high side)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1076 (Fuel injection pump metering valve) with FMI 6 (Current too high; short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU when the turbocharger wastegate/bypass actuator circuit or its commanded response is abnormal. Typical causes are a failed coil/solenoid, corroded or chafed wiring, or the actuator mechanically sticking.
source_doc: DTC list EMRL1 main + secondary ECU

short_description: Common rail (fuel) pressure sensor circuit reads high (shorted to supply)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1239 (Common rail (fuel) pressure sensor) with FMI 3 (Circuit voltage high / short to supply) is set by the Engine ECU when the fuel rail (common rail) pressure sensor signal leaves its plausible window or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. Typical causes are a failed sensor, corroded connector pins, chafed harness wiring, or a genuine underlying system condition the sensor is correctly reporting.
source_doc: DTC list EMRL1 main + secondary ECU

short_description: CAN bus communication fault (general) needs the OEM's special diagnostic procedure
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1669 (CAN bus communication fault (general)) with FMI 14 (See manufacturer-specific instructions) is set by the Engine ECU on an OEM-proprietary CAN channel or internal module link, rather than the main vehicle J1939 backbone -- a 'Machine' or implement CAN segment, a smart sensor's or actuator's own link to its controlling module, a tractor-trailer bridge, or a processor-to-processor link inside the ECU. Typical causes are a fault on that dedicated sub-network's wiring or connector, the linked smart device itself failing, or an internal ECU hardware fault that only a component replacement resolves.
source_doc: DTC list EMR5 / MD1 (2026-07-22)

short_description: NOx sensor, upstream of SCR reads in-range but abnormally high
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3216 (NOx sensor, upstream of SCR) with FMI 0 (Reading in-range but far too high) is set by the Engine ECU for the NOx sensor mounted ahead of the SCR catalyst (measuring engine-out NOx). The fault covers open/short circuits, communication loss to the smart sensor, heater faults, offset/drift error, or the sensor reporting itself removed from the exhaust stream.
source_doc: DTC list EMR5 / MD1 (2026-07-22)

short_description: DPF differential pressure sensor flagged with an OEM-specific fault code (reserved FMI)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3251 (DPF differential pressure sensor) with FMI 30 (Reserved by SAE; some OEMs assign proprietary meanings) is set by the Engine ECU when it detects an internal fault in its own memory, software or supply. Typical causes are a corrupted calibration, a power/ground fault at the ECU connector, or, rarely, a failed ECU that needs dealer replacement and reprogramming.
source_doc: DTC list EMRL1 main + secondary ECU

short_description: ECU sensor supply voltage 4, out-of-range fault reads in-range but abnormally low
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3512 (ECU sensor supply voltage 4, out-of-range fault) with FMI 1 (Reading in-range but far too low) is set by the Engine ECU when the 5V/8V sensor supply rail reads outside its expected voltage band. Typical causes are a shorted sensor or harness branch overloading the shared supply, a corroded connector, or a failed regulator/relay.
source_doc: DTC list EMR5 / MD1 (2026-07-22)

short_description: DPF/SCR regeneration status (backup/standby/inhibited) AdBlue defrosting actuator fault
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3719 (DPF/SCR regeneration status (backup/standby/inhibited)) with FMI 15 (Slightly above normal range) is set by the Engine ECU for the DEF tank's freeze-protection heating valve or defrost circuit. DEF freezes below about 12 F (-11 C), so the tank carries a coolant-fed or electric heater circuit with its own valve; a stuck-open valve, an air pocket in the DEF line after a freeze/thaw cycle, or an electrical fault in the valve circuit land in this family.
source_doc: DTC list EMRL1 main + secondary ECU

short_description: DEF supply line heater circuit output current critically high
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 4340 (DEF supply line heater circuit) with FMI 27 (Reserved by SAE; some OEMs assign proprietary meanings) is set by the Engine ECU for one of the electric heater circuits on the DEF supply, return, suction or backflow hoses (open circuit, short to ground, short to battery, or critical overcurrent). These heaters keep DEF from freezing in the lines below ambient; a failed heater does not stop the truck from running but will set an inducement path if DEF cannot be pumped in cold weather.
source_doc: DTC list EMRL1 main + secondary ECU

short_description: Exhaust gas temperature sensor (SCR inlet/outlet) circuit open
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 4363 (Exhaust gas temperature sensor (SCR inlet/outlet)) with FMI 14 (See manufacturer-specific instructions) is set by the Engine ECU when an SCR catalyst exhaust gas temperature sensor (upstream or downstream of the catalyst brick) reads open, shorted, out of plausible range, or critically overtemperature. The SCR dosing strategy will not dose (or will derate) without a trusted catalyst temperature window, so this fault frequently rides along with a NOx conversion or inducement fault.
source_doc: DTC list EMRL1 main + secondary ECU

short_description: Oil pressure / cold-engine indicator lamp circuit voltage reads high (shorted to supply)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 5099 (Oil pressure / cold-engine indicator lamp) with FMI 3 (Circuit voltage high / short to supply) is set by the Engine ECU when the dashboard warning lamp or indicator output circuit reads an abnormal voltage or current. Typical causes are a burned-out bulb/LED, a corroded connector, or a short/open in the wiring between the module and the indicator.
source_doc: DTC list EMR5 / MD1 (2026-07-22)

short_description: DEF suction line heater circuit fault detected, root cause not yet isolated

detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 7107 (DEF dosing pump circuit) with FMI 10 (Value changing implausibly fast or slow) is set by the Engine ECU for the DEF supply module's pump: pressure that will not build, will not hold, or reads erratic, a pump motor drive fault, or a supply voltage/temperature fault on the pump module itself. A clogged inlet strainer in the tank or air drawn in through a loose suction fitting are common causes that mimic a failed pump.

Typical causes are a failed sensor, corroded connector pins, chafed harness wiring, or a genuine underlying system condition the sensor is correctly reporting.

short_description: Deutz parameter 520321: Component reports an internal failure
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520321 (Deutz parameter 520321 (role not stated)) is a Deutz-specific parameter with no plain-language description in the source OEM tables; FMI 12 (Smart device or component defective) reported by the Engine ECU indicates an internal device or calibration fault. Typical causes are a corrupted calibration, an internal module fault, or a configuration step that was skipped after service; a Deutz dealer tool is usually needed to identify the exact component behind this parameter.

detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 524147 (Deutz parameter 524147 (role not stated)) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the Engine ECU when the DEF line/system pressure sensor circuit is faulted, out of calibration, or the pressure it reports cannot be regulated to target (mechanical system fault). This is the sensor and regulation loop, distinct from the pump itself.
source_doc: KWP list EMR4 (2026-06-10)

short_description: Secondary accelerator pedal position sensor message not received at the expected rate
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 29 (Secondary accelerator pedal position sensor) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the Transmission when a value the engine control system broadcasts on J1939 -- engine speed, torque, accelerator pedal position, an idle/torque limit, or an engine configuration message -- stops arriving at the expected rate, fails validation, or is out of the receiving controller's calibrated range. The Transmission only receives this value over the network rather than measuring it directly, so the fault is a link problem until the engine ECU's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the engine ECU for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Transmission itself has failed.

short_description: Park brake switch message not received at the expected rate
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 70 (Park brake switch) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the Transmission when a value the body controller or a dash/cab-mounted switch broadcasts on J1939 stops arriving at the expected rate or fails validation. The Transmission only receives this value over the network rather than reading the switch directly, so the fault is a link problem until the body controller's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the body controller for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Transmission itself has failed.

short_description: Transmission countershaft speed signal frequency, pulse width or period abnormal
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 160 (Transmission countershaft speed) with FMI 8 (Wrong frequency, pulse width or period) is set by the Transmission when the countershaft speed sensor signal is erratic, out of frequency, drifting, below its plausible range, or reads an open/shorted circuit. This sensor is used for clutchless shift timing and synchronizer protection.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Engine idle speed / configuration message reading below the normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 188 (Engine idle speed / configuration message) with FMI 1 (Reading in-range but far too low) is set by the Transmission when a value the engine control system broadcasts on J1939 -- engine speed, torque, accelerator pedal position, an idle/torque limit, or an engine configuration message -- stops arriving at the expected rate, fails validation, or is out of the receiving controller's calibrated range. The Transmission only receives this value over the network rather than measuring it directly, so the fault is a link problem until the engine ECU's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the engine ECU for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Transmission itself has failed.

short_description: Transmission selected gear reported by the module as internally defective
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 524 (Transmission selected gear) with FMI 12 (Smart device or component defective) is the TECU's own internal gear and direction tracking logic (current, selected or requested gear, or a commanded-vs-actual direction mismatch) reporting a device fault or failing to update at the expected message rate. This is typically a downstream symptom of an unresolved rail, range or clutch fault elsewhere in the transmission rather than a fault of its own.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Cruise control active status: stored calibration values are out of range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 595 (Cruise control active status) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the Transmission when a value from the cruise control or Automated Driving System (ADS) stops arriving at the expected rate or fails validation -- a primary/secondary ADS command, an ADS operation-status report, or a cruise resume/pause command. The Transmission only receives this value over the network rather than generating it directly, so the fault is a link problem until the sending controller's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the ADS/cruise source controller for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Transmission itself has failed.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Engine control unit internal fault flagged as a network reporting error
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 629 (Engine control unit internal fault) with FMI 19 (Network-received value flagged as error) is an internal TECU self-check or watchdog fault, set when the module's own operation is outside its expected range, timing or state. It is not tied to a single external circuit, so rule out power, ground and network faults first before treating it as a module problem.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Transmission reverse gear output circuit open, current too low
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 767 (Transmission reverse gear output) with FMI 5 (Current too low; open circuit) is set by the Transmission when the TECU's neutral or reverse output signal (used to drive back-up lights, neutral-safety interlocks or similar chassis functions) reads an open circuit, a short to power or ground, or the TECU cannot confirm the output reached its commanded state.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 787 (Transmission inertia brake solenoid) with FMI 6 (Current too high; short to ground) is set by the Transmission when the driveline inertia brake solenoid, used to slow the countershaft for clutchless upshifts, reads an electrical fault, an out-of-range response, or fails a calibration check.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Starter enable relay circuit voltage low (shorted to ground)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1321 (Starter enable relay circuit) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Transmission when the TECU-controlled relay that enables engine cranking only in neutral reads an open or shorted drive circuit, or is mechanically stuck.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: PTO 1 request signal stored calibration values are out of range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3452 (PTO 1 request signal) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the Transmission when the driver's PTO request input (a dash switch or multiplexed request) reads a circuit fault, a calibration issue, or a message that is not arriving at the expected rate.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: PTO 2 engage signal flagged under a manufacturer-specific fault condition
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3457 (PTO 2 engage signal) with FMI 14 (See manufacturer-specific instructions) is set by the Transmission when the PTO engagement air solenoid reads an electrical fault (open, short, out-of-range) or the PTO fails to mechanically engage as commanded.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Primary automatic drive selector (ADS) signal stored calibration values are out of range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3651 (Primary automatic drive selector (ADS) signal) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the Transmission when a value from the cruise control or Automated Driving System (ADS) stops arriving at the expected rate or fails validation -- a primary/secondary ADS command, an ADS operation-status report, or a cruise resume/pause command. The Transmission only receives this value over the network rather than generating it directly, so the fault is a link problem until the sending controller's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the ADS/cruise source controller for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Transmission itself has failed.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Auxiliary transmission range switch circuit voltage low (shorted to ground)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3960 (Auxiliary transmission range switch) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Transmission when the driver's auxiliary range-select switch reads a circuit fault, a calibration issue, or the TECU's confirmed auxiliary gear status message is not arriving at the expected rate or does not match the commanded range.
source_page: Fault Code 983: Auxiliary Trans Range Switch
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Shift rail B position sensor reading below the normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 4219 (Shift rail B position sensor) with FMI 1 (Reading in-range but far too low) is set by the Transmission when a shift rail position sensor reads out of range, erratic, drifting, or an open/shorted circuit, so the TECU cannot confirm which rail position (gear) is actually selected.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Shift rail C position sensor reading moderately above the normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 4220 (Shift rail C position sensor) with FMI 16 (Moderately above normal range) is set by the Transmission when a shift rail position sensor reads out of range, erratic, drifting, or an open/shorted circuit, so the TECU cannot confirm which rail position (gear) is actually selected.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Clutch engage solenoid 2 circuit voltage low (shorted to ground)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 5615 (Clutch engage solenoid 2) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Transmission when one of the clutch engage or release solenoids reads an open circuit, a short to power or ground, an out-of-range coil resistance, or fails to respond at the commanded frequency. These solenoids meter shop air to the clutch actuator, so an electrical fault here directly stops clutch engagement or release.
source_page: Fault Code 512: Clutch Engage Solenoid 2 (C3) – Fine Vent
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Shift rail A, fore solenoid circuit open, current too low
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 5900 (Shift rail A, fore solenoid) with FMI 5 (Current too low; open circuit) is set by the Transmission when one of the X-Y shift rail fore/aft solenoids reads an electrical fault (open, short, out-of-range) or fails to move the rail as commanded, preventing the TECU from selecting or confirming the requested gear.
source_page: Fault Code 576: Rail A Fore Solenoid (A3)
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Shift rail D, fore solenoid circuit current above the normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 5903 (Shift rail D, fore solenoid) with FMI 0 (Reading in-range but far too high) is set by the Transmission when one of the X-Y shift rail fore/aft solenoids reads an electrical fault (open, short, out-of-range) or fails to move the rail as commanded, preventing the TECU from selecting or confirming the requested gear.
source_page: Fault Code 636: Rail D Fore Solenoid (C2)

short_description: Shift rail B, aft solenoid logged with no further diagnostic detail available
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 5909 (Shift rail B, aft solenoid) with FMI 31 (Fault present; no further detail) is set by the Transmission when one of the X-Y shift rail fore/aft solenoids reads an electrical fault (open, short, out-of-range) or fails to move the rail as commanded, preventing the TECU from selecting or confirming the requested gear.
source_page: Fault Code 597: Rail B Aft Solenoid (A1)
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Shift rail D position sensor reading slightly above the normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 5941 (Shift rail D position sensor) with FMI 15 (Slightly above normal range) is set by the Transmission when a shift rail position sensor reads out of range, erratic, drifting, or an open/shorted circuit, so the TECU cannot confirm which rail position (gear) is actually selected.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Shift rail D calibration value drifting upward over time
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 5954 (Shift rail D calibration) with FMI 20 (Value has drifted upward over time) is set by the Transmission when a shift rail's stored calibration end-points have drifted out of limits, or a mechanical condition prevents the rail from completing its calibration stroke.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Shift rail C operation status: value drifting upward over time
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 6146 (Shift rail C operation status) with FMI 20 (Value has drifted upward over time) is set by the Transmission when a shift rail does not reach or hold the commanded position within the expected time or range, indicating a mechanical shift-quality problem (binding synchronizer, worn shift fork, low air pressure) rather than a wiring fault.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Alternate shift schedule selector circuit voltage high (shorted to supply)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 6160 (Alternate shift schedule selector) with FMI 3 (Circuit voltage high / short to supply) is set by the Transmission when the dash-mounted switch that selects an alternate shift schedule, secondary operating mode or rail road mode reads an electrical fault (open, short, stuck contact), a calibration outside limits, or the TECU cannot confirm the switch state at the expected message rate.
source_page: Fault Code 977: Alternate Shift Schedule Selector
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Rail-road (hi-rail) mode switch stored calibration values are out of range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 7941 (Rail-road (hi-rail) mode switch) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the Transmission when the dash-mounted switch that selects an alternate shift schedule, secondary operating mode or rail road mode reads an electrical fault (open, short, stuck contact), a calibration outside limits, or the TECU cannot confirm the switch state at the expected message rate.
source_page: Fault Code 965: Rail Road Mode Switch
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Secondary automatic drive selector (ADS) operation status: stored calibration values are out of range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 20874 (Secondary automatic drive selector (ADS) operation status) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the Transmission when a value from the cruise control or Automated Driving System (ADS) stops arriving at the expected rate or fails validation -- a primary/secondary ADS command, an ADS operation-status report, or a cruise resume/pause command. The Transmission only receives this value over the network rather than generating it directly, so the fault is a link problem until the sending controller's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the ADS/cruise source controller for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Transmission itself has failed.
source_page: Fault Code 126: Secondary ADS Operation Status
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Intake manifold air temperature, shorted to supply (voltage high)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 105 (Intake manifold air temperature) with FMI 3 (Circuit voltage high / short to supply) is set by the Engine ECU when the intake or charge-air temperature sensor signal leaves its plausible window or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. Typical causes are a failed sensor, corroded connector pins, chafed harness wiring, or a genuine underlying system condition the sensor is correctly reporting.
source_doc: OMRG35856 PowerTech DTC list

short_description: Controller ignition/battery input voltage, moderately below normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 627 (Controller ignition/battery input voltage) with FMI 18 (Moderately below normal range) is set by the Engine ECU when the battery/system supply voltage reads outside its expected range. Typical causes are a weak/failed battery, a failed alternator, a slipping drive belt, or corroded battery/ground connections.
source_doc: OMH229936 9670/9770 STS engine control unit DTCs

short_description: Injector cylinder 3, calibration data invalid
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 653 (Injector cylinder 3) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the Engine ECU when the fuel injector driver circuit reads an abnormal current, resistance or calibration value. Typical causes are a failed injector coil/solenoid, a chafed or corroded driver circuit, or an injector trim code that was not carried over after replacement.
source_doc: OMH229936 9670/9770 STS engine control unit DTCs

short_description: Engine control unit (ECU) internal temperature, reading far too high (most severe)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1136 (Engine control unit (ECU) internal temperature) with FMI 0 (Reading in-range but far too high) is set by the Engine ECU when it detects an internal fault in its own memory, software or supply. Typical causes are a corrupted calibration, a power/ground fault at the ECU connector, or, rarely, a failed ECU that needs dealer replacement and reprogramming.
source_doc: OMRG35856 PowerTech DTC list

short_description: EGR valve 2 position sensor, calibration data invalid
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3822 (EGR valve 2 position sensor) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the Engine ECU when the EGR valve actuator will not reach or hold a commanded position, reports an internal fault, loses calibration, or the motor coil circuit is open or shorted. Carbon buildup in the valve bore that increases actuator load is a leading mechanical cause behind an electrical-looking fault.
source_doc: OMH229936 9670/9770 STS engine control unit DTCs

short_description: Exterior light relay driver circuit is shorted to ground or drawing excess current
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 2368 (Parameter 2368 (role not stated by the OEM tables)) with FMI 6 (Current too high; short to ground) is set by the Body controller when the relay driver stage for a lighting circuit does not read the coil current it expects. Typical causes are a failed relay, a corroded relay socket connector, or an open or shorted driver wire between the body controller and the relay coil.
source_doc: S08327 Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Codes (2010)

short_description: Windshield wiper motor circuit is open, no current detected
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 4057 (Windshield wiper motor circuit) with FMI 5 (Current too low; open circuit) is set by the Body controller when the wiper motor output circuit reads open or shorted rather than the expected motor load. Typical causes are a failed or seized wiper motor, binding wiper linkage that overloads the motor, or a corroded connector or damaged wiring between the body controller and the motor.
source_doc: S08327 Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Codes (2010)

short_description: Remote power module 7, channel 2 output does not match the commanded state
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520542 (Remote power module 7, channel 2 output) with FMI 2 (Signal unstable, intermittent or implausible) is set by the Body controller when a Remote Power Module (RPM) output channel reports a state the ESC does not expect for the load configured on that channel — open, shorted to ground, or not updating. Typical causes are a failed load device, a corroded connector at the RPM or the load, or damaged wiring on that channel's circuit.
source_doc: S08327 Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Codes (2010)

short_description: Body controller switch input circuit is erratic or intermittent
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520674 (Body controller switch input circuit) with FMI 2 (Signal unstable, intermittent or implausible) is set by the Body controller when a discrete switch input (a clutch, neutral, lock, mode, power, or similar panel or chassis switch) reads a state the ESC considers implausible, or a switch is found stuck in one position against the vehicle's actual operating state. Typical causes are a worn or failed switch, a corroded connector or pin, or an open or shorted signal wire between the switch and the body controller.
source_doc: S08327 Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Codes (2010)

short_description: Dash indicator LED circuit is open, no current detected
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520816 (Dash indicator LED circuit) with FMI 5 (Current too low; open circuit) is set by the Body controller when a dash-mounted indicator or telltale lamp output (wait-to-start, change-oil, filter-restriction, or similar) reads open or shorted rather than the expected bulb or LED load. Typical causes are a failed indicator bulb or LED, a corroded connector behind the dash, or damaged wiring between the body controller and the indicator.
source_doc: S08327 Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Codes (2010)

short_description: Intake air temperature sensor 1 reading out of expected range for conditions
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 172 (Intake air temperature sensor) with FMI 10 (Value changing implausibly fast or slow) is set by the Engine ECU when the intake or charge-air temperature sensor signal leaves its plausible window or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. Typical causes are a failed sensor, corroded connector pins, chafed harness wiring, or a genuine underlying system condition the sensor is correctly reporting.
source_doc: PSI 6.0L OBD-HD engine diagnostic manual (FCCC chassis)

short_description: Ignition coil A primary circuit reads low (shorted to ground)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1268 (Ignition coil A primary circuit) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU when the ignition coil circuit or its commanded response is abnormal. Typical causes are a failed coil/solenoid, corroded or chafed wiring, or the actuator mechanically sticking.
source_doc: PSI 6.0L OBD-HD engine diagnostic manual (FCCC chassis)

short_description: Oxygen sensor, bank 1 sensor 1, circuit reads low voltage
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3217 (Oxygen (O2) sensor, bank 1 sensor 1) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU for the lambda (wideband O2) sensor used to trim the aftertreatment/combustion feedback loop, or for a post-catalyst fuel trim that has moved outside its expected band. A lazy or contaminated sensor and an exhaust leak ahead of the sensor are the most common causes on gasoline- and dual-fuel heavy-duty engines with a three-way or oxidation catalyst.
source_doc: PSI 6.0L OBD-HD engine diagnostic manual (FCCC chassis)

short_description: Fuel system slightly too rich at idle, bank 2
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 4239 (Fuel trim, bank 2 (lean/rich)) with FMI 17 (Slightly below normal range) is set by the Engine ECU when the bank fuel-trim monitor signal leaves its plausible window or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. Typical causes are a failed sensor, corroded connector pins, chafed harness wiring, or a genuine underlying system condition the sensor is correctly reporting.
source_doc: PSI 6.0L OBD-HD engine diagnostic manual (FCCC chassis)

short_description: Barometric pressure sensor circuit reads high (shorted to supply)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 108 (Barometric pressure sensor) with FMI 3 (Circuit voltage high / short to supply) is set by the Engine ECU when the ambient/barometric pressure sensor signal leaves its plausible window or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. Typical causes are a failed sensor, corroded connector pins, chafed harness wiring, or a genuine underlying system condition the sensor is correctly reporting.
source_doc: SEBU8601-07 1206E-E70TTA industrial engine OMM, Table 3 diagnostic codes

short_description: EGR flow does not match the expected temperature response (valve mechanically stuck or misadjusted)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 2659 (EGR flow/temperature mismatch) with FMI 7 (Mechanical part not reacting or misadjusted) is set by the Engine ECU when the pressure differential across the EGR circuit (or the fresh-air temperature downstream of the EGR cooler) is implausible or high. A fouled or internally leaking EGR cooler, a plugged EGR orifice, or a genuine differential pressure sensor fault are the usual causes.
source_doc: SEBU8601-07 1206E-E70TTA industrial engine OMM, Table 3 diagnostic codes

short_description: Parameter 3837: value reading moderately below the normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3837 (Parameter 3837 (role not stated by the OEM tables)) is a Perkins-specific parameter with no plain-language description in the source OEM tables; FMI 18 (Moderately below normal range) reported by the Engine ECU indicates a circuit-type electrical fault (open, short or out-of-range voltage) on whatever sensor or actuator this parameter represents. Diagnose it as a wiring/connector fault using the OEM pin-out for this SPN rather than assuming a specific component.
source_doc: SEBU8601-07 1206E-E70TTA industrial engine OMM, Table 3 diagnostic codes

short_description: Pneumatic governor valve (3/2-way) circuit: open, current too low
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 705 (Auxiliary I/O channel 5) with FMI 5 (Current too low; open circuit) is set by the ABS/ESC on a configurable auxiliary output driver -- wired at the factory to a differential lock, transfer case, trailer, or a general-purpose 3/2 valve solenoid -- when that output circuit reads shorted to voltage or ground, open, or does not match its parameter-set configuration. Diagnosis follows the wiring for whichever solenoid the output is assigned to on this vehicle.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: Wheel-speed sensor frequency too high; check for corroded or damaged wiring (drive axle left)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 791 (Wheel speed sensor, drive axle left) with FMI 12 (Smart device or component defective) is set by the ABS/ESC when a wheel-speed sensor circuit reads open, shorted to voltage or ground, or the sensor no longer reports as a valid device to the ECU. Typical causes are a broken or corroded sensor connector, a chafed harness near the axle or suspension travel, a failed sensor coil, or a wiring short at the ECU pin.
source_doc: MM0112 ABS/ESC E-version maintenance manual (05.2020)

short_description: Abnormal wheel-speed signal; check sensor spring clip and mounting block (additional axle right)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 794 (Wheel speed sensor, additional axle right) with FMI 11 (Fault detected, cause undetermined) is set by the ABS/ESC when a wheel-speed signal is plausible in amplitude but behaves erratically -- chattering, jumping, arriving at the wrong update rate, or disagreeing with the other wheels on the axle, including a sensor pair wired in reverse or an output too low at drive-off. Typical causes are a damaged or debris-packed tone ring, a loose sensor, mismatched tire sizes on an axle, or a mis-wired sensor after a service.
source_doc: MM0112 ABS/ESC E-version maintenance manual (05.2020)

short_description: Brake demand sensor, secondary circuit: FBV wiring fault (interruption or short) suspected
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1068 (Brake demand sensor, secondary circuit) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the ABS/ESC when the dual-channel brake demand (foot/treadle valve) sensor that reports how hard the driver is braking reads an implausible offset, an open primary or secondary circuit, or has not completed its calibration. This is the sensor at the brake pedal or treadle valve, not a wheel sensor.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: Steering angle parameter external timeout fault: routine timed out during EOL execution
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520247 (Steering angle parameter external timeout fault) with FMI 31 (Fault present; no further detail) is set by the ABS/ESC when the vehicle's end-of-line (EOL) configuration -- the number and type of wheel-speed sensors and modulators, the ESC enable/disable setting, or a steering-angle learning parameter -- no longer matches what is wired on the truck. This follows a component swap, an ECU replacement, or a parameter reset and needs a dealer-level diagnostic tool, not a parts fix.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: Wheel-speed plausibility, axle 5 right: sudden downward jump in wheel-speed reading
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520510 (Wheel-speed plausibility, axle 5 right) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the ABS/ESC when a wheel-speed signal is plausible in amplitude but behaves erratically -- chattering, jumping, arriving at the wrong update rate, or disagreeing with the other wheels on the axle, including a sensor pair wired in reverse or an output too low at drive-off. Typical causes are a damaged or debris-packed tone ring, a loose sensor, mismatched tire sizes on an axle, or a mis-wired sensor after a service.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: ABS valve overheating protection (thermal cutoff): approaching over-temperature prewarning threshold
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520530 (ABS valve overheating protection (thermal cutoff)) with FMI 15 (Slightly above normal range) is set by the ABS/ESC when an ABS modulator valve's coil has run hot enough, for long enough, to trip its thermal protection -- a normal slightly-above-range flag at the low level, a fault flag at the critical level. Excessive ABS cycling from a bad wheel-speed signal, a partially shorted coil drawing extra current, or a valve stuck partially open all raise coil temperature.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: EEPROM parameter block 1 fails checksum verification, ECU may use a default value
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 524270 (EEPROM parameter block 1 checksum fault) with FMI 7 (Mechanical part not reacting or misadjusted) is set by the ABS/ESC when a checksum on one of its stored EEPROM parameter groups -- traction control, brake configuration, gravity/vehicle setup, axle configuration -- fails, meaning the ECU's own configuration memory is corrupted. This is an internal ECU fault, not a wiring problem.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: ECU received an invalid intake air temperature value over the network
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 172 (Intake air temperature sensor) with FMI 19 (Network-received value flagged as error) is set by the Aftertreatment DCU for an internal dosing control unit fault: SPI communication between internal chips, an A/D converter, internal overtemperature, an EEPROM read/write/erase failure, or the module reporting it has entered a backup/limp mode. These are module-internal faults; there is no field repair beyond DCU replacement once wiring and grounds are ruled out.
source_doc: Troubleshooting manual, engines over 56 kW (2024)

short_description: DCU internal supply voltage reads high (rail/check 1)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 523558 (DCU internal supply voltage, rail/check 1-2) with FMI 3 (Circuit voltage high / short to supply) is set by the Aftertreatment DCU for the dosing control unit's own supply voltage, main relay, or sensor-supply circuit (over/under-voltage, relay sticking or opening early). Check battery voltage, ground straps and the DCU's main relay before condemning the module.
source_doc: Troubleshooting manual, engines over 56 kW (2024)

short_description: Supply module pressure dropping abnormally
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 523627 (Supply module pressure level) with FMI 1 (Reading in-range but far too low) is set by the Aftertreatment DCU for the DEF supply module's pump: pressure that will not build, will not hold, or reads erratic, a pump motor drive fault, or a supply voltage/temperature fault on the pump module itself. A clogged inlet strainer in the tank or air drawn in through a loose suction fitting are common causes that mimic a failed pump.
source_doc: Troubleshooting manual, engines over 56 kW (2024)

short_description: Injector cylinder 1 driver discharge switch stuck open
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 651 (Injector cylinder 1) with FMI 12 (Smart device or component defective) is set by the Engine ECU when the fuel injector driver circuit reads an abnormal current, resistance or calibration value. Typical causes are a failed injector coil/solenoid, a chafed or corroded driver circuit, or an injector trim code that was not carried over after replacement.
source_doc: Troubleshooting manual, engines over 56 kW (2024)

short_description: MSC inter-microcontroller communication fault
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 518267 (MSC inter-microcontroller communication link) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the Engine ECU on an OEM-proprietary CAN channel or internal module link, rather than the main vehicle J1939 backbone -- a 'Machine' or implement CAN segment, a smart sensor's or actuator's own link to its controlling module, a tractor-trailer bridge, or a processor-to-processor link inside the ECU. Typical causes are a fault on that dedicated sub-network's wiring or connector, the linked smart device itself failing, or an internal ECU hardware fault that only a component replacement resolves.
source_doc: Troubleshooting manual, engines over 56 kW (2024)
